title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

issues_found: All three opponents — the Muslim rivals of Zaragoza, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona, and the defenders of Valencia — are collapsed into a single SARACEN player, so the Christian Catalan army at Tevar fights with Saracen architecture and CAMEL_RIDER units. Barcelona could and should have been a separate Spanish (or Frankish/Teutonic) player.

Berenguer Ramon II appears only as a renamed generic unit inside a Saracen roster; the engine ships no hero for him, but placing him under a Muslim civilization compounds the substitution with a cultural error.

The first mission, 'drive off the raiders threatening Zaragoza', is a generic invented engagement in place of a documented episode such as Almenar (1082) or Morella, where El Cid actually fought for al-Mu'tamin against al-Mundir and Berenguer Ramon II.
El Cid's ally, the Hudid king of Zaragoza (al-Mu'tamin/al-Musta'in), is never placed as a unit or player at all — the patron whose service defines 1081-1086 exists only in narration text.
The defeat condition kills El Cid in battle, whereas he died of natural causes in Valencia in 1099; acceptable as a campaign stake but not a historical outcome.

Only 107 objects on a 120x120 map: Zaragoza, Tevar and Valencia are all represented by the single Player 2 town centre/castle complex rather than as distinct locations, so the geography of the exile is not really depicted.
